title: CAFEIN – Federated Learning Platform
summary: CERN reports that its CAFEIN federated learning platform is in operational use; in a test on a public stroke dataset, federated training outperformed training on local data alone.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: CAFEIN is a federated learning platform developed at CERN. It uses federated averaging (FedAvg) to train models across locally held datasets, with secure aggregation and privacy protections. In a preprint of 2 October 2024, CERN staff and their co-developers at Politecnico di Milano and the Italian National Research Council describe the platform built for clinical sites in the EU TRUSTroke stroke project. They tested it on a public stroke dataset split across three simulated nodes. They report that federated training with FedAvg performed better than training on local data alone. They describe the platform as ready for deployment in hospitals. In a submission to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), current as of June 2025, CERN describes the platform as operationally used. Its intended benefit is collaborative model-assisted analysis without centralizing sensitive records. No source quantifies an analytical gain for a partner institution or a resulting patient outcome. No source reports a clinical result or an independent evaluation.
purpose: Support collaborative model-assisted research while keeping sensitive data local.
location: European clinical centers in the TRUSTroke stroke project
